summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested in 2012, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Patrick de Silva Kularatne (1893–1976) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at University College London and the University of London around 1913 to 1917, and later served as principal of Ananda College from circa 1918 to 1943.

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu and Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje, and taught disciples such as Shenphen Nangwa and Terton Sogyal.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a position at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and served at Emory University (attested in 1998; Professor Emeritus attested in 2026).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1997) as well as traditional teachers Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Geshe Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Sorbonne, he directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1965–1980) and held a chair at the EPHE from 1981.

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (PhD circa 1876), taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (1879–1881), and worked at Open Court Publishing Company from 1887 to 1919.

Paul Copp specializes in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser (attested 2005) and held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago (attested 2014 and 2026).

Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a doctorate at Yale. He served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949) and director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a figure in Buddhist studies. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954, also serving as a board member), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. His posts included directing at Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1930) and the Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin. He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin (1881–1887), RWTH Aachen University (circa 1887–1889), and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1976 to 2017 and served as head of the Pali Text Society.

Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (circa 1952–1954) and Adelphi University (circa 1954–1958). He held an academic post at the University of California, San Francisco from circa 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter (born 1939) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (circa 1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (circa 1968–1972), and served at Union Theological Seminary from circa 2007 to 2017.

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Liège. He served as professor at the University of Liège (circa 1879–1883) and Ghent University (from 1883), where he became rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin and Paul Dundas. He holds a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University, where he served in the Center for Buddhist Studies (2003) and as Lecturer in Classical Tibetan (2016).
